name: Sediment Strata Monument
brief: Terre d'Hermès as geological time: a flat screen-printed poster of hard-edge sedimentary strata bands - pale sky, sand, ochre, sienna, deep umber - stacked like a core sample, with one thin flint-orange seam marking the burial line. The upright flacon stands centred as the monument extracted from those layers, its baked high-key speculars untouched by the flat ink world. All type stacks in the calm pale sky band at the top: tracked Baskerville brand line, the name in one generous serif line, closed by a short printed rule like a survey mark. No floor, no horizon - pure stratigraphic narrative against clear glass and amber juice.
material: screen-printed matte paper with hard-edge sedimentary strata bands
lighting: perfectly even shadowless frontal illumination, flat graphic ink light with no falloff

background.prompt: Seamless flat screen-printed matte paper poster of horizontal sedimentary strata bands in pale bone, sand, ochre, burnt sienna and deep umber stacked from top to bottom, one thin hard-edge flint-orange seam line between the ochre and sienna bands, perfectly even shadowless illumination, no texture gradients, no objects

initial_spec.lighting: perfectly even shadowless frontal illumination, flat graphic ink light with no falloff

name: Salt Flat Dawn Mirror
brief: The juice returned to its mineral origin: a photographic dawn salt plain where a continuous cracked crust sweeps to a low horizon exactly at the true base line, cool mist-grey sky above. The cutout stands right of centre on that crust, its measured contact shadow settling into the white mineral cracks, while the left half stays calm for a wrapped Arial Narrow column: brand at column head, the name across two tall lines, a short rust rule closing the column like a survey stake. Vertical overlap with the shoulder but wide horizontal clearance keeps the editorial grid honest; cold salt matte against warm amber liquid is the entire temperature story.
material: cracked salt crust plain under a hazy dawn sky
lighting: soft overcast dawn daylight, diffuse cool frontal with no hard shadows, matching the baked studio light

background.prompt: Vast cracked white salt crust plain meeting a pale hazy mist-grey sky at a low horizontal horizon nine tenths down the frame, fine polygonal crust cracks across a continuous flat ground, cool diffuse dawn light, matte mineral grain, no objects

initial_spec.lighting: soft overcast dawn daylight, diffuse cool frontal with no hard shadows, matching the baked studio light

name: Ember Horizon Night Field
brief: Night over worked earth: a flat matte ink-night card carrying one oversized hard-edge burnt-ember half-disc rising from the bottom edge, its crown passing behind the flacon's shoulders like a buried sun, crossed by one thin orange seam at the disc crown. The cutout is lifted into the upper two-thirds so the ember field below becomes a quiet plaque band: tracked geometric-sans brand line, then the name set wide and centred in Century Gothic capitals near band width, closed by a short rule floating between image and text like a print registration mark. No floor, no horizon - pure rising-disc geometry against translucent amber glass.
material: flat matte ink-night card with hard-edge printed ember half-disc
lighting: perfectly even shadowless frontal illumination, flat graphic ink light with no falloff

name: Flint Gallery Oblique
brief: A constructed mineral gallery: one monolithic cleft flint wall in cool bone-grey stone meets a continuous honed pale stone ground at a horizon aligned with the true base line, while a single crisp oblique shadow edge rakes the wall from upper left like late sun through a gallery slot. The cutout stands left of centre on that ground, contact shadow anchoring its foot, while the right wall stays calm for a wrapped Times column: brand at column head, the name across two tall serif lines, a short rust rule closing the column like a chisel mark. Vertical overlap with the shoulder but wide horizontal clearance keeps the two-column grid deliberate; cold split-stone matte against warm amber juice reads as earth under architecture.
material: cleft flint stone wall with honed pale stone ground
lighting: bright directional late-day light casting one crisp oblique shadow edge on the wall, warm ambient on the ground
